svg.text: Single server, 5 writer threads plus edge builders, per protocol

g.text: 5 writer tasks on a pool of 10
5 writer tasks on a pool of 10
from User / Photo, so the edge
The whole load run happens once per client protocol, so both wire paths carry the same work.
@EnumSource(DatabaseWrapper.Protocol.class) -> HTTP (2480) and GRPC (50051); one container per invocation
A plain single-server container: no Raft, no quorum, nothing between the client and the storage engine.
Five tasks each open their own connection and write 1000 users with 10 photos apiece.
Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10); each task: new DatabaseWrapper(...) - addUserAndPhotos(1000, 10) - close()
Two more tasks build the edges, and they read back ids first - an edge needs vertices that already exist.
createFriendships(500) and createLike(500); TypeIdSupplier pages ids out of User / Photo as it goes
While the pool drains, the test thread polls the counts every five seconds and logs them.
Nothing here is awaited or approximated: the pool has terminated, so every expected row must exist.
The run ends by dumping Micrometer: per-operation timers and the error counters the wrappers increment.
